prompt_text: Design a collaborative real-time document editing system (like Google Docs) that must support: (1) offline editing with later sync, (2) conflict resolution when multiple users edit the same paragraph, (3) end-to-end encryption so the server cannot read document contents. Describe your data structures, sync protocol, and conflict resolution strategy.
response:
A collaborative real-time document editing system requires careful design of data structures, synchronization, and security.

Data structures: The document is represented as a conflict-free replicated data type (CRDT) or operational transformation (OT) sequence. Each character or chunk has a unique ID (e.g., Lamport timestamp or UUID) and maintains references to predecessor and successor nodes. This allows concurrent edits to merge deterministically without locks.

Sync protocol: Clients maintain a WebSocket connection to an operational transformation server. Local edits are immediately applied to the local CRDT and broadcast as operations (insert/delete with position IDs) to the server, which validates ordering and relays to other clients. For offline support, the client logs operations locally; upon reconnection, it replays the log and applies server operations that arrived in the interim, using the CRDT merge function to resolve conflicts.

End-to-end encryption: The document content is encrypted on the client using a symmetric key derived from a user passphrase or key-exchange protocol (e.g., Double Ratchet). The server stores and synchronizes only encrypted blobs and operation metadata (position IDs, timestamps). It cannot decrypt content. Key distribution among collaborators occurs out-of-band or via a separate key-server with zero-knowledge architecture.

Conflict resolution: When two users edit the same paragraph concurrently, the CRDT merge preserves both insertions in a deterministic total order (e.g., by author ID tie-breaker). Deletions are tombstoned so that concurrent insertions at deleted positions remain valid. The UI surfaces concurrent edits with subtle cursors and attribution rather than blocking.
